claims.topic: PKCanvasViewDelegate surface: no payload, no cause
claims.final_claim: PKCanvasViewDelegate is @MainActor and exposes exactly five optional callbacks: canvasViewDrawingDidChange, canvasViewDidFinishRendering, canvasViewSelectionDidChange, canvasViewDidBeginUsingTool and canvasViewDidEndUsingTool. Each one receives only the PKCanvasView. None carries a diff, the affected stroke IDs, or a cause such as stroke, erase, undo or paste.
claims.os_sdk: iOS/iPadOS 13.0+ for the protocol and drawing/tool callbacks. The selection callback page also lists 13.0, but WWDC26 presents it as new in iOS 27 (see E1-14). Checked against the iOS 27 SDK docs.
claims.evidence_excerpt: "@MainActor protocol PKCanvasViewDelegate : UIScrollViewDelegate" ... "optional func canvasViewDrawingDidChange(_ canvasView: PKCanvasView)" — "Tells the delegate that the contents of the current drawing changed." Overview: "determine the start- and end-of-event sequences using the currently selected tool, and determine when those events affect the drawn content."

claims.topic: When drawingDidChange is final for a stroke
claims.final_claim: canvasViewDidEndUsingTool fires on pencil or touch up, but the drawing is not complete at that moment. Apple says a later canvasViewDrawingDidChange arrives after the final (delayed) force values, and only then is the drawing guaranteed final.
claims.os_sdk: iOS/iPadOS 13+. The behaviour was described in 2019 and has not been re-stated for 27.
claims.evidence_excerpt: "On pencil or touch up, you'll get a canvasViewDidEndUsingTool callback. However, at this point, your drawing is not yet fully updated because ... it's not until those final force values come in, that you get a final canvasViewDrawingDidChange. Only at this point, you're guaranteed to have a final finished drawing."

claims.topic: drawingDidChange frequency per stroke / erase / undo
claims.final_claim: Apple does not document how many times drawingDidChange fires for one ink stroke, for a continuous bitmap-eraser drag, for a lasso move, or for one undo or redo. It also gives no way to tell these cases apart from inside the callback.
claims.evidence_excerpt: The doc page has only the abstract "Tells the delegate that the contents of the current drawing changed." and a parameter description. It has no Discussion section about frequency or cause.

claims.topic: canvasViewDidFinishRendering and scroll/zoom
claims.final_claim: canvasViewDidFinishRendering is a rendering-readiness signal, not an edit signal. It fires when a new drawing is assigned, on zoom, and on scroll. Because PKCanvasViewDelegate inherits UIScrollViewDelegate, the app also receives standard scroll and zoom callbacks.
claims.evidence_excerpt: "The PKCanvasView object calls this method when you assign a new drawing to its drawing property, when the user zooms in on the canvas, or when the canvas scrolls." WWDC19: "it's not until those tiles are done loading that you'll get a canvasViewDidFinishRendering callback. You'll also get this callback after scrolling or zooming."

claims.topic: Programmatic drawing assignment vs learner edits
claims.final_claim: The claim is inferred. A community repo (BoardBlog, created 2022-05-27, iOS 15 era) reports that assigning canvasView.drawing re-triggers canvasViewDrawingDidChange. Apple's PencilKitDraw sample wraps programmatic assignment in a manual registerUndo, which suggests PencilKit registers no undo for programmatic assignment. Apple's iOS 27 handwriting sample (TutorModel.replay) assigns canvasView.drawing.strokes on the live canvas at about 60 fps during replay and registers no undo. A community PaperKit 27 project (simulator only, 2026-09-20) reports that assigning PaperMarkupViewController.markup 'calls the delegate twice, synchronously'.
claims.verifier_note: The source date is wrong. GitHub API gives created_at 2022-05-27 and pushed_at 2022-06-06, not 'undated iOS 13/14 era'. Sample code verified from https://docs-assets.developer.apple.com/published/d18940fcfc4f/DrawingWithPencilKit.zip: DrawingViewController.swift lines 148-155 (setNewDrawingUndoable), LICENSE 'Copyright © 2024 Apple Inc.'. iOS 27 sample verified from https://docs-assets.developer.apple.com/published/48bcc5ceffcb/BuildingAHandwritingRecognitionExperienceWithPencilKit.zip, TutorModel.swift lines 68-104. Community PaperKit note from commit messages in https://github.com/MarcusJinuChang/NoteCode/pull/15 (simulator only, finger touches). No Apple doc states either behaviour. The origin=app flag recommendation stands, and it must handle bursts of about 60 writes per second.
claims.os_sdk: The sample targets iOS 13+ (LICENSE copyright 2024). Community report is undated (iOS 13/14 era). Not re-verified on 27.
claims.evidence_excerpt: BoardBlog README: "This line of code [canvasView.drawing = pkDrawing] causes the canvasViewDrawingDidChange method to be executed (again)". Apple sample DrawingViewController.swift: "/// Helper method to set a new drawing, with an undo action to go back to the old one. func setNewDrawingUndoable(_ newDrawing: PKDrawing) { let oldDrawing = canvasView.drawing; undoManager?.registerUndo(withTarget: self) { $0.setNewDrawingUndoable(oldDrawing) }; canvasView.drawing = newDrawing }"

claims.topic: PencilKit undo uses the responder-chain UndoManager
claims.final_claim: Apple does not document how PencilKit registers undo. The evidence suggests built-in ink undo lives on the responder-chain UndoManager, which by default is the window's. That evidence: UIResponder.undoManager returns the nearest shared manager and the window supplies one; the tool picker has built-in undo/redo buttons; Apple's sample binds its compact-mode undo:/redo: buttons to First Responder; forum users see the tool picker's undo count track strokes. Whether PKCanvasView honours an undoManager override on a hosting view controller is unknown.

sources.date: thread from iOS 14 beta era (2020); archived 2024

claims.evidence_excerpt: UIResponder.undoManager: "Returns the nearest shared undo manager in the responder chain ... By default, every window of an application has an undo manager ... You may add undo managers to your view controllers to perform undo and redo operations local to the managed view." Forum 651788: "The undo buttons in the PKToolPicker will reflect what seems like an accurate number of undos (ie if I have 5 strokes I can tap undo 5 times ...)". Main.storyboard: <action selector="undo:" destination="dkx-z0-nzr"/> where dkx-z0-nzr = IBFirstResponder.

claims.topic: UndoManager notifications usable for undo/redo labelling
claims.final_claim: UndoManager (@MainActor) posts WillUndoChange/DidUndoChange and WillRedoChange/DidRedoChange with no userInfo, on the actor, thread or queue that calls undo()/redo(). It also posts Checkpoint, DidOpenUndoGroup and WillCloseUndoGroup/DidCloseUndoGroup. It exposes isUndoing, isRedoing, canUndo, canRedo, undoActionName/redoActionName, undoCount and redoCount (iOS 17.4+ only), undoActionIsDiscardable, and undoActionUserInfoValue(forKey:) (iOS 18+). iOS/iPadOS 26 adds typed messages such as UndoManager.DidUndoChangeMessage with groupIsDiscardable. None of these identifies the strokes that changed.
claims.verifier_note: Verified: NSUndoManagerDidUndoChange Discussion ('This notification doesn't contain a userInfo dictionary. The system posts this notification on the actor, thread, or dispatch queue that calls undo().'). DidUndoChangeMessage is iOS 26.0 with init(groupIsDiscardable:). undoCount lists iOS 17.4, and its doc warns: 'A nonzero value doesn't imply you can safely invoke undo() immediately, because you may have to close open undo groups first.' The os_sdk field omitted the 17.4 floor for undoCount/redoCount, which does not matter for 26/27 targets. Whether PencilKit mutates the drawing synchronously inside undo() (so that isUndoing is true inside drawingDidChange) and whether it sets undoActionName are both undocumented and need a device test.
claims.evidence_excerpt: NSUndoManagerDidUndoChange: "If you invoke undo() or undoNestedGroup(), this notification is posted. The notification object is the UndoManager object. This notification doesn't contain a userInfo dictionary. The system posts this notification on the actor, thread, or dispatch queue that calls undo()." isUndoing: "true if the manager is performing its undo() or undoNestedGroup() method".

claims.topic: Undo entry points (burst undo)
claims.final_claim: Built-in undo/redo reaches the canvas from several sources. (a) PKToolPicker's palette buttons, in regular size class only; Apple's sample, copyright 2024, still says compact size class has none. (b) Apple Pencil Pro squeeze: the WWDC24 undo slider is available in all apps even without PKToolPicker, can be suppressed with a UIPencilInteraction squeeze delegate, and is not sent to the app if the user's squeeze preference is 'run shortcut'. UIPencilPreferredAction.showContextualPalette also shows 'undo and redo options if tools aren't available'. (c) System editing sources: shake-to-edit (applicationSupportsShakeToEdit defaults to true), three-finger editing gestures (UIResponder.editingInteractionConfiguration, iOS 13+), hardware-keyboard Cmd-Z, and the iPadOS 26 main menu (UIMainMenuSystem, iOS 26). Any of them can produce rapid multi-step undo/redo.
claims.verifier_note: WWDC24 10214 (2024-06-11) quote verified verbatim. The session demonstrates squeeze → long-press the undo button → slider. The os_sdk '17.5/18+' is not supported: WWDC24 presents the slider in the iOS 18 cycle, and 17.5 availability was not verified. Apple Support https://support.apple.com/guide/ipad/draw-with-apple-pencil-ipadc55b6c7a/ipados (iPadOS 27 page): 'you can squeeze the barrel of the pencil to quickly perform an action such as undo or show the tool palette'. The compact-size statement comes from WWDC19 and the sample comment; it was not re-verified against the iOS 18+ tool picker redesign.
claims.os_sdk: Tool picker undo: iPadOS 13+. Squeeze slider: iPadOS 17.5/18+ with Apple Pencil Pro.
claims.evidence_excerpt: WWDC19: "in the regular size class that undo/redo buttons are actually baked inside of the palette ... in the compact size class, they're not in the palette at all." WWDC24: "the squeeze gesture can be used to access a slider for quickly working through undo/redo history. This is available in all apps; even if you don't use PKToolPicker. If you want to suppress this behavior, install a UIPencilInteraction with a delegate that implements the method to respond to squeeze actions."

claims.topic: Mutating canvas drawing breaks built-in undo
claims.final_claim: Community forum reports from 2020 (iOS 14 beta, thread 651788, workaround and FB7794075 from the original poster) say that mutating canvasView.drawing directly (strokes.append, replacing strokes, remove/insert, changing masks) breaks or resets PencilKit's built-in undo: undo taps do nothing. A 2022 reply in thread 718677 repeats this second-hand; its author says they 'haven't really got to the undo/redo stage'. There is no Apple staff answer, and nothing has been re-verified on 26/27.
claims.verifier_note: Quotes verified in Wayback snapshots, whose dates were mislabelled. 651788 snapshot is 2022-07-21 (https://web.archive.org/web/20220721181028/https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/651788). 718677 snapshot is 2023-03-04 (https://web.archive.org/web/20230304234639/https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/718677). Neither is from 2024. The 718677 quote is hearsay-level evidence, so 'pasting' as a trigger is unconfirmed. The OP's workaround (groupsByEvent=false plus per-stroke registerUndo) reportedly worked only partially. The design conclusion (a read-only observer that never writes the learner's live drawing) still holds as a precaution.
claims.os_sdk: Reported on iOS 14 beta and 16.1. Not re-verified on 26/27.
claims.evidence_excerpt: 651788: "If you have a PKCanvasView and call canvasView.drawing.strokes.append(myNewStroke), it renders the UndoManager unusable, or at least makes it start fresh ... those undo presses won't actually do anything." 718677: "by modifying the PKDrawing directly you confuses the default UndoManager, and therefore may have to implement your own undo stack."

claims.topic: Eraser types
claims.final_claim: PKEraserTool.EraserType.vector removes the whole line it touches. .bitmap removes only the touched portions. .fixedWidthBitmap (iOS 16.4+) has no documented abstract. Eraser width is configurable from 16.4.
claims.os_sdk: vector/bitmap: iOS 13.0+. fixedWidthBitmap and width: iOS/iPadOS 16.4+.
claims.evidence_excerpt: vector: "When a vector eraser touches any portion of a drawn line, it removes the entire line." bitmap: "An eraser that removes only those portions of the drawing it touches." fixedWidthBitmap: (no abstract).

claims.topic: Bitmap (pixel) erase = mask + split into independent strokes
claims.final_claim: PencilKit represents partial (pixel) erasure with a pre-transform mask on PKStroke. The mask can make holes, or cut the stroke into separate independent strokes, each with its own transform and mask. Paths are not masked. maskedPathRanges gives the parametric ranges of the path that intersect the mask, but it is not the same as the visible ink: a still-visible fragment can have zero maskedPathRanges if it does not intersect the path spline.
claims.verifier_note: WWDC20 10148 (2020-06-23) verified verbatim, including: 'Strokes can have zero masked ranges. For example, if the user erases all but a fraction of a stroke, and that fraction does not intersect the path spline, then the resulting masked stroke will have zero maskedPathRanges.' The iOS 27 restatement in WWDC26 203 is verified. mask and maskedPathRanges are iOS 14.0+. The claim's phrase 'the visible parts must be read through maskedPathRanges' overstates this. Store the mask itself (UIBezierPath) as the evidence of what was erased, not only the ranges.
claims.os_sdk: mask and maskedPathRanges: iOS 14+. Re-stated for iOS 27.
claims.evidence_excerpt: WWDC20: "Masked strokes are typically created when the pixel eraser is used to erase only a portion of a stroke ... Masks can have holes. Or they can cut a stroke into multiple pieces ... the stroke has been split into two separate strokes. These become unique, independent strokes and behave as such to the user and in the API ... each of these two new strokes has its own separate transform and mask." WWDC26: "PencilKit represents partial erasure using a mask. When the pixel eraser removes part of a stroke, the remaining visible portions are defined by a mask."

claims.topic: Stable stroke identity (iOS 27)
claims.final_claim: In iOS/iPadOS 27, PKStroke.id (UUID, get/set) and PKStrokePath.id (UUID, get-only) arrive with Identifiable conformance. Apple describes the ID as stable across transforms, edits and undo operations. PKStroke and PKStrokePath are not Equatable; PKDrawing is Equatable, Codable and Sendable.
claims.evidence_excerpt: PKStroke.id: "var id: UUID { get set }" — "The unique identity of the stroke." PKStrokePath.id warning: "Using multiple stroke paths with identical IDs but different control points will result in undefined rendering behavior." WWDC26: "PKStroke and PKStrokePath both gain conformance to the Identifiable protocol. It is a stable UUID, so you can track a stroke across transforms, edits, and undo operations."

claims.topic: Unknowns about ID behaviour
claims.final_claim: Apple does not document: which IDs the pieces of a pixel-erase split get (original ID kept, new IDs, or a shared path.id); whether pasted or duplicated strokes get new IDs; whether stroke IDs survive dataRepresentation() and init(data:) round trips; or what IDs strokes drawn on iPadOS 26 get when loaded on 27.
claims.evidence_excerpt: PKStroke.id has only the abstract "The unique identity of the stroke." PKContentVersion.version5 (27.0): "The version that adds stroke render state support." Neither page says anything about ID persistence or split lineage.

claims.topic: Selection APIs (iOS 27)
claims.final_claim: PKCanvasView.selection (Set<UUID>, get/set) is new in 27.0 and lets the app read and set which strokes are selected. canvasViewSelectionDidChange fires whenever the user's selection changes. Its doc page lists iOS 13.0 availability, which looks like a metadata inconsistency, since WWDC26 introduces it as new.
claims.os_sdk: selection: iOS/iPadOS 27.0+. Delegate method: doc metadata says 13.0; WWDC26 presents it as new in 27.
claims.evidence_excerpt: selection: "var selection: Set<UUID> { get set }" — "The identifiers of the strokes selected on the canvas." WWDC26: "you can now control the selection state on PKCanvasView. There's also a new delegate method, canvasViewSelectionDidChange, that fires whenever the user's selection changes."

claims.topic: Lasso move/rotate/scale = PKStroke.transform
claims.final_claim: The expectation is that a lasso move changes PKStroke.transform and leaves the path points unchanged. Apple says the transform gives a stroke's orientation and position, and that users can select and move one split piece without affecting the other. Apple does not explicitly say that lasso edits write to transform rather than to the path.
claims.evidence_excerpt: transform: "The affine transform of the stroke after rendering." WWDC20: "A transform gives the orientation and position of the stroke ... The user can select one of the strokes and move it around without affecting the other stroke."

claims.topic: Per-stroke timing
claims.final_claim: Each stroke path has a creationDate, and each point has a timeOffset in seconds from that date. Strokes are stored in drawing order. Apple's iOS 27 sample still sorts by path.creationDate when replaying writing order. Erasures, transforms and undos carry no timestamp inside the model.
claims.evidence_excerpt: timeOffset: "The time offset since the start of the stroke path in seconds." WWDC20: "Time offset is the offset in seconds from the creation date of the stroke path ... These strokes are in the order that the user drew them". Sample: "let sorted = canvasView.drawing.strokes.sorted { $0.path.creationDate < $1.path.creationDate }"

claims.topic: Programmatic erase / slicing (iOS 27)
claims.final_claim: iOS 27 adds PKDrawing.erasePath(_:mask:transform:), which mutates the drawing, and erasingPath(_:mask:transform:), which returns a new drawing. Both apply a PKStrokePath as an eraser, 'just as if the user had used the eraser tool'. It also adds PKStroke.substroke(range:). Apple warns that slicing can be expensive and suggests running it off the main thread.
claims.evidence_excerpt: "mutating func erasePath(_ eraserPath: PKStrokePath, mask: UIBezierPath? = nil, transform: CGAffineTransform = .identity)" (no abstract). WWDC26: "It cuts through the drawing, slicing a single stroke into multiple independent strokes with their own mask, just as if the user had used the eraser tool on the canvas ... slicing can be expensive on complex drawings ... consider erasing on a background thread".

claims.topic: No operation-log API
claims.final_claim: No public operation history exists. PKCanvasView, PKDrawing, PKCanvasViewDelegate, PKToolPickerObserver, PaperMarkupViewController.Delegate and PaperMarkup expose no list of operations, no undo-stack contents and no change records. UndoManager exposes only counts, flags and action names.
claims.evidence_excerpt: PKCanvasView topic groups (complete): delegate; tool, isRulerActive, allowsFingerDrawing (deprecated), drawingPolicy; drawingGestureRecognizer; drawing; selection; maximumSupportedContentVersion; isDrawingEnabled. None of these is a history API. UndoManager: "undoCount", "redoCount", "undoActionName" ("Returns an empty string ... if no action name has been assigned").

claims.topic: PaperKit change reporting (26+)
claims.final_claim: PaperMarkupViewController.Delegate (iOS/iPadOS 26.0+) has paperMarkupViewControllerDidChangeMarkup, DidChangeSelection, DidBeginDrawing and DidChangeContentVisibleFrame. None carries a payload, and there is no DidEndDrawing. iOS 27 adds three adornment callbacks. The controller conforms to Observable and declares 'override dynamic var undoManager: UndoManager? { get }', which has no documentation. It is not documented as controller-owned. Community testing on the 27 simulator found that it walks the responder chain, putting ink undo on a sibling text view's stack. The controller is a non-open class, so an undoManager override needs a container view controller.
claims.verifier_note: The delegate method list is verified; all four methods are iOS 26.0. The implication 'undo manager is controller-owned, which makes observing undo there cleaner' is refuted by community evidence and was never documented. Source: NoteCode PR #15 commit of 2026-09-19 (simulator, finger touches only), https://github.com/MarcusJinuChang/NoteCode/pull/15. The Delegate protocol is declared 'protocol Delegate : AnyObject' with no @MainActor in the docs. The same community notes also say 'There's no end-of-stroke callback, so save from didChangeMarkup'.
claims.evidence_excerpt: "paperMarkupViewControllerDidChangeMarkup(_:) — Tells the delegate when the markup changes." PaperMarkupViewController overview: "Properties are observable, so to save markup changes to disk, iterate over the changes to markup." undoManager: "@MainActor @preconcurrency override dynamic var undoManager: UndoManager? { get }"

claims.topic: PaperKit element model is 27-only; opaque on 26
claims.final_claim: PaperMarkup.subelements (MarkupOrderedSet), PaperMarkup.id, MarkupOrderedSet (including strokes: [PKStroke] and subscript(id: UUID) -> PKStroke?), MarkupOrderedSet.ElementID (.stroke(UUID), init from a stroke UUID), PaperMarkupViewController.selection and MarkupInteractions all require 27.0. On iPadOS 26, PaperMarkup has bounds, contentsRenderFrame, featureSet, indexableContent (async String?), dataRepresentation, draw(in:frame:options:) (async), append(contentsOf:) (PaperMarkup or PKDrawing), transformContent, removeContentUnsupported and insertNew* methods, but no element enumeration.

claims.topic: PaperKit adornments and interaction locks
claims.final_claim: In iOS 27, MarkupAdornment overlays are separate from the persisted markup, so they are never saved, printed or exported. MarkupInteractions can make individual elements read-only (for example a problem template) or restrict move, resize, rotate, style, delete and select.

claims.topic: Tool-change observation
claims.final_claim: PKToolPickerObserver.toolPickerSelectedToolItemDidChange (iOS 18+) replaces toolPickerSelectedToolDidChange, which is deprecated at 18.0. PKCanvasView conforms to PKToolPickerObserver. Once it is added with toolPicker.addObserver(canvasView), 'the canvas automatically updates its drawing environment accordingly.' That canvasView.tool read at DidBeginUsingTool is the tool that actually made the change is inferred, not documented. It fails if the canvas is not registered as an observer, and it does not cover PKToolPickerCustomItem tools (iOS 18+), which PKCanvasView does not draw with.
claims.verifier_note: The observer docs are verified verbatim. The automatic update requires explicit registration: WWDC19 says 'We'll add the Canvas View as an observer'. Timing of tool updates relative to DidBegin (for example Pencil double-tap switching to the eraser mid-sequence) needs a device test.
claims.os_sdk: toolPickerSelectedToolItemDidChange: iOS/iPadOS 18.0+. Old method deprecated at 18.0.
claims.evidence_excerpt: "Each time the user changes the selected tool or other drawing characteristics, the tool picker notifies any registered observers." PKCanvasView: "A canvas view conforms to the PKToolPickerObserver protocol ... the canvas automatically updates its drawing environment accordingly."

claims.topic: Threading and snapshot handling
claims.final_claim: PKCanvasViewDelegate, PKToolPickerObserver and UndoManager are @MainActor. PaperMarkupViewController is @MainActor, but its nested Delegate protocol is declared without @MainActor in the docs. PKDrawing, PKStroke and PKStrokePath are Sendable value types. WWDC19 says drawing-derived work such as thumbnails can safely run on a background queue. PKStrokeRecognizer is a 'final actor' (27.0+), and Apple advises throttling it.
claims.verifier_note: Verified from declarations and transcripts. iOS 26 also adds async, nonisolated(nonsending) PKDrawing.draw(in:frame:from:darkUserInterfaceStyle:) and PaperMarkup.draw(in:frame:options:), which render a snapshot without the canvas.
claims.evidence_excerpt: WWDC19: "Because all of these values have value types, we can safely do this work on a background queue." PKDrawing conforms to: Decodable, Encodable, Equatable, Sendable. WWDC26: "PKStrokeRecognizer is a Swift actor ... consider throttling your calls ... Updating the results on every stroke may use more power than you need".

claims.topic: Persistence cost and content versioning
claims.final_claim: Apple gives no cost guidance for PKDrawing.dataRepresentation(), which returns 'the entire contents of the drawing', so latency and size for large drawings must be measured on device. Serialized drawings carry a required content version: version4 (26.0) adds Reed Pen ink and version5 (27.0) adds stroke render state. canvas maximumSupportedContentVersion limits which edits the canvas allows.

claims.final_claim: The canvas's copy, paste, duplicate and delete actions (via UIEditMenuInteraction and responder paste: since iPadOS 16.1) add or remove strokes without a pencil-driven tool bracket. What IDs pasted strokes receive, and whether these actions fire DidBegin/EndUsingTool, is not documented.

verifier_added.topic: New PKStroke/PKStrokePath initializers mint fresh IDs
verifier_added.claim: On 27, the full PKStroke initializer defaults to 'id: UUID = UUID()', and PKStrokePath has init(controlPoints:creationDate:id:). verifier_added.claim: After a pixel erase, a stroke fragment that is still visible can have zero maskedPathRanges, because the remaining sliver does not intersect the path spline. Evidence of what remains visible must therefore store the mask geometry and/or a rendered image, not only the path ranges.

verifier_added.topic: Overlapping stroke brackets due to delayed force
verifier_added.claim: Apple warns that final force values keep arriving after the Pencil lifts, and that the user can start the next stroke before the previous one is final. In PencilKit this likely means a stroke's trailing drawingDidChange can arrive after the next DidBeginUsingTool, so brackets overlap and attribution must be by diff and creationDate, not strict bracket nesting. The PencilKit consequence is inferred from a general Pencil statement.
verifier_added.os_sdk: iPadOS 13+ with pressure-sensing Apple Pencil (not re-stated for 26/27)
verifier_added.evidence_excerpt: "There's a region of the stroke that's still waiting for those final force values. You need to keep listening to them even after touch has ended. Now, one aspect of this is that it means that the user can start drawing the next stroke before the last stroke has got all the final values."

verifier_added.topic: PaperKit 27 community findings on undo, assignment and merge
verifier_added.claim: Community testing on the iOS 27 simulator with finger touches only reports four things. PaperMarkupViewController's undoManager walks the responder chain, so ink undo landed on a sibling UITextView's stack. The class cannot be subclassed, so a container view controller has to supply its own undoManager. Assigning markup fires the delegate twice, synchronously. Assigning a markup merges into the canvas rather than replacing it, and there is no end-of-stroke callback. These findings need confirming on a device with Apple Pencil.

dimensions.design_recommendation:
Use PKCanvasView as the structured-evidence canvas on both 26 and 27. On 27, optionally host it inside PaperKit, where element IDs equal PKStroke.id. On iPadOS 26, PaperKit markup is opaque; only blob versions are possible.

Record history as an append-only log kept by an observer that never changes the learner's ink (see E1-09).

1) Envelope for every event:
- device_id and install-scoped seq, a UInt64 that is persisted and never reused
- canvas_id, attempt_id, session_id
- mono_ts (ContinuousClock) and wall_ts
- os_build and api_tier (26 = fingerprint identity, 27 = stable UUID)
- origin: learner_tool | undo | redo | app | unattributed
- evidence: observed facts only

2) Capture on the main actor: record DidBeginUsingTool/DidEndUsingTool with a snapshot of canvasView.tool. Observe canvasView.undoManager Will/Did Undo/Redo notifications and read isUndoing/isRedoing inside drawingDidChange. Log selection changes (27), scroll/zoom (UIScrollViewDelegate) and app lifecycle. On each drawingDidChange, copy the Sendable PKDrawing and enqueue it to a serial background actor. Do nothing else on main.

3) The actor diffs the new drawing against the last committed snapshot.
- On 27, key strokes by PKStroke.id.
- On 26, key by a fingerprint: path.creationDate + point count + first/last point + ink + randomSeed. Tag these events identity=fingerprint (lower confidence).
- Output: added IDs, removed IDs, and modified IDs with the fields that changed (transform, mask/maskedPathRanges, ink, path.id, renderGroupID).
- Empty diffs are dropped, which handles the extra callback from late force updates.

4) Labels come only from correlation, never from guessing:
- write: additions inside an inking-tool bracket, with path.creationDate inside the bracket
- erase_vector / erase_bitmap: removals, or mask changes/splits, inside an eraser bracket of that type
- transform: transform-only changes on selected IDs (lasso or edit menu)
- undo / redo: a diff inside the undo/redo bracket, recorded with undoCount/redoCount after the step
- app: our own assignments, flagged before we write
- anything else: unattributed_change
Never store reasons such as "corrected mistake" or "gave up".

5) Immutable original ink: the first time a stroke ID or version is seen, write it once as a content-addressed record (stroke data, unmasked path, creationDate, timeOffsets, ink, randomSeed, renderState). Erasure, masking or undo only adds new versions and never overwrites. Keep split lineage (piece to parent via shared path.id/creationDate) as a derived fact until the device test confirms it. Write a full PKDrawing dataRepresentation checkpoint every N events and at attempt boundaries, off the main thread, with requiredContentVersion.

6) Branches and attempts:
- Branch: derive it from facts. A write committed while redoCount > 0 immediately before it discards the redo stack; record the branch_from seq and the IDs of the discarded redo state.
- Abandon/retry and new attempt: record only from explicit learner UI actions (for example "try again", "new attempt"). Never infer them from erasing.

7) Gaps: log a gap event with reason whenever continuity cannot be vouched for:
- backgrounding, scene disconnect, or canvas not visible or not first responder
- a drawing reload, or the diff queue backing up
- an identity downgrade (26 fingerprint collision)
- a failed checkpoint

8) Scope honesty: this structured path covers only our own canvas. That is the A45 fallback, or product-owned ink layers, and it does not satisfy R59/A44 on its own. Reuse the same event schema for any other product-owned ink surface; for example, a future Safari-extension ink layer would use web Pointer Events instead of PencilKit.
experiment_steps_proposed: Build an instrumented harness app (Xcode 27, 27A266a) and run it on iPadOS 27.0 (24A437) and on one iPadOS 26.x iPad, with Apple Pencil (Pro if available). For every delegate callback, UndoManager notification, selection change and scroll/zoom event, log the monotonic timestamp, a main-thread assertion, canvasView.tool, the stroke-ID set (27) or fingerprint set (26), and isUndoing/isRedoing.

Single pen stroke, Pencil and finger (drawingPolicy .anyInput): count drawingDidChange calls per stroke and their timing relative to DidEndUsingTool. Check whether any call arrives mid-stroke and whether the stroke's points or force change between calls. Watch for the 'Missed updates at end of stroke' console message.

Vector erase of one stroke; bitmap and fixedWidthBitmap erase through the middle of one stroke; a long continuous bitmap drag across 10 strokes. For each, record callback counts, the removed and added stroke IDs, whether pieces keep the original PKStroke.id or share path.id and creationDate, the masks, and maskedPathRanges.

Lasso select then move/rotate/scale: confirm which field changes (transform vs path points), that IDs and path.id stay stable, the number of canvasViewSelectionDidChange calls, and whether setting canvasView.selection from code fires the callback. Check whether lasso and eraser gestures fire DidBegin/DidEndUsingTool.

Undo/redo from each source: tool picker buttons, three-finger swipe/double-tap, hardware keyboard Cmd-Z/Shift-Cmd-Z, and the Apple Pencil Pro squeeze undo slider (multi-step). Record the notification sequence (Will/Did Undo/Redo, Checkpoint, Will/DidCloseUndoGroup), whether drawingDidChange fires synchronously between Will and Did with isUndoing == true, undoCount/redoCount and undoActionName, and whether undoing a bitmap erase restores the original stroke ID(s).

Undo manager identity: compare canvasView.undoManager with window.undoManager and the hosting view controller's. Override undoManager on the hosting view controller and check whether PencilKit registers ink undo there. Put a UITextField in the same window and confirm its undo is isolated.

Programmatic changes: assign canvasView.drawing, and append via canvasView.drawing.strokes. Check whether drawingDidChange fires, whether any undo is registered (canUndo/undoCount), and whether the built-in undo stack still works afterwards on 27.
Edit menu (UIEditMenuInteraction) copy/paste/duplicate/delete: IDs of pasted or duplicated strokes (new or copied), callback sequence, and undo registration.

Persistence: round-trip dataRepresentation()/init(data:) and check that PKStroke.id and PKStrokePath.id are preserved across app relaunch. Load a drawing created on iPadOS 26 into 27 and record which IDs appear and whether they are stable across repeated loads. Measure dataRepresentation latency and size and diff CPU time for 50/500/2000-stroke drawings on the target iPad, on and off the main thread.

PaperKit (27): embed PaperMarkupViewController with PKToolPicker. Count paperMarkupViewControllerDidChangeMarkup calls per stroke, erase, undo and lasso move. Confirm subelements.strokes IDs match PKStroke.id and survive undo. Observe its undoManager notifications. On iPadOS 26, confirm there is no element enumeration (only dataRepresentation).

Lifecycle and gaps: draw, then background the app, use Slide Over or Stage Manager, or move the canvas off-screen. Check whether callbacks or undo can occur while not first responder, and confirm the logger emits gap events. Run the recorder under XCTest to check that seq numbers stay strictly monotonic across crash or relaunch (persisted counter).

claims.topic: SCFrameStatus on iOS 27
claims.final_claim: All six SCFrameStatus cases are public on iOS/iPadOS 27.0: complete, idle, blank, suspended, started, stopped. So each delivered screen sample can say whether it holds new content or is a 'no change' / blank / suspended / stopped marker.

Platforms for the idle case: iOS 27.0, iPadOS 27.0, Mac Catalyst 18.2, macOS 12.3, tvOS 27.0, visionOS 27.0.

claims.topic: queueDepth and slow handlers

Apple's WWDC22 guidance: holding surfaces longer than minimumFrameInterval x (queueDepth-1) makes ScreenCaptureKit stall and miss frames. On iOS the pool size is system-chosen and unknown, so a slow or retaining handler will drop frames silently.

dimensions.design_recommendation:
Scope: treat E2 as observation only. Evidence is 'what pixels showed at time t', never 'what the app or learner did'.

1) Capture adapters and one schema
- iPadOS 27: SCContentSharingPicker.present() for full display, UIBackgroundModes screen-capture. Test variants with and without an active audio session.
- iPadOS 26, and as a fallback on 27 until the device test clears E2-11: broadcast upload extension.
- Every evidence record carries: capture_path, stream_id, output_px, native_px, scale, displayTime (synchronizationClock timebase), and frame status.

2) Handler discipline (no queueDepth or frame-rate control on iOS)
- In the SCStreamOutput callback, on a dedicated serial queue (not .main), read the attachments: status, displayTime, contentRect, scaleFactor/contentScale.
- For .complete frames, make a 1/8-scale luma thumbnail and a per-tile hash (for example 32x32-px tiles at native size), copy out, and release the buffer immediately.
- Never keep IOSurfaces.
- Log displayTime deltas. A delta above 2x the median delivered interval while the status is complete counts as a 'drop' micro-gap.

3) Keyframe policy (the app does its own change detection, since dirtyRects is macOS-only)
- a) Change-settle keyframe: when changed tiles go quiet for about 400-600 ms, copy one native-resolution frame and encode it losslessly or near-losslessly (HEIC/PNG, CPU or hardware encoder, background-safe). Store it with the changed-tile mask relative to the previous keyframe.
- b) Large-change keyframe: when more than about 40% of tiles change within one frame (scroll, page or problem change, app switch), take a keyframe right away and mark 'global_change'. Do not label it scroll, undo or page-change unless separate evidence exists: a visible page indicator by OCR, a URL/tab change from the Safari extension, or our own anchor events.
- c) Heartbeat: while frames or .idle markers keep arriving, advance last_confirmed_unchanged_at without storing pixels. If neither arrives for more than 2 s, the state is 'unknown/stale', not 'unchanged'.
- d) Action-triggered clip (iOS 27 only): on explicit learner actions (ask for help, check work, change problem, stop sharing), call SCClipBufferingOutput.exportClip for up to 15 s. Record the interval it actually covers. On iPadOS 26, attach the last K keyframes instead and label them 'keyframe history'.
- e) An AI request gets the freshest keyframe with its age. If the age is above the threshold (for example 3 s) or the stream is inactive, the request is sent as 'stale view' or blocked. No silent substitution.

4) Freshness and gap bookkeeping (append-only timeline). Gap kinds:
- not_sharing, picker_cancelled, user_stopped, system_stopped, inactive, app_suspended/no_frames, status_blank, status_suspended, frame_drop.
- possibly_obscured (uniform black regions, FairPlay, apps hiding under capture).
- own_ui_occlusion (our overlay covering the external app).
- low_legibility (output scale below 1 or OCR confidence under threshold).
- analysis_deferred (background Neural Engine/GPU restriction).
- Each gap has start, end (or 'open'), cause source (API signal or heuristic) and a confidence value.

5) What pixels may and may not claim
- Allowed:
  - 'Region R showed ink/content C (as keyframe K) at t1.'
  - 'Between observed frames t1 and t2, ink in R appeared, disappeared or changed.'
  - 'The whole view changed at t (global_change).'
  - 'The view was unchanged from t1 to t2 (confirmed by frames/idle).'
  - 'Nothing is known between t1 and t2 (gap).'
  - A machine transcription of pixels, labelled as such with its confidence.
- Forbidden without separate evidence:
  - Undo vs erase vs redo vs lasso-delete vs page change vs scroll. E2-21 shows these look identical.
  - Notability's or Canvas's internal state or undo stack.
  - 'The learner abandoned or retried because...', or any intent.
  - Any statement about intervals inside a gap.
  - Attributing to the external app any pixel change that matches our own strokes (E2-23).

6) Privacy and honesty
- Keep the capture indicator visible, and make stop one tap.
- Stop all buffering and exports on userStopped.
- Default to on-device-only storage of keyframes. Upload only frames attached to an AI request.
- Continuous SCRecordingOutput only as an explicit opt-in.
experiment_steps_proposed: Background survival (top priority, iPad Air M3 and iPad Pro M5 on iPadOS 27.0 24A437). Build a probe app with SCContentSharingPicker.present(), UIBackgroundModes screen-capture, and NSScreenCaptureUsageDescription if Xcode 27 requires it. Run variants A (no audio session) and B (audio background mode plus an active playAndRecord session as in Apple's sample). Switch to Notability, Canvas Student and Safari for 15 minutes each. Log per-sample wall time, displayTime, status, contentRect, scaleFactor, contentScale and buffer dimensions. Report whether frames keep flowing, when the app is suspended, and any didStopWithError codes. Reproduce the LensLink report (E2-11).

Delivered rate and idle semantics. With the screen static for 60 s, then continuous Pencil writing in Notability for 60 s, then Safari scrolling for 60 s, measure delivered fps (checking for a 60 or 120 Hz ceiling on Pro M5 ProMotion), the count of .idle versus .complete samples, the longest silence without callbacks, and whether .started, .blank or .suspended appear on lock, Control Center, notification banners, Split View and Stage Manager changes, or rotation.

Slow-handler test. Add artificial delays of 0, 20, 50, 100 and 250 ms to the handler, and a variant that retains 1, 2 or 3 CMSampleBuffers. Measure displayTime gaps, dropped frames, stalls and recovery. This determines the effective iOS surface-pool size and a safe per-frame budget.

Resolution and legibility. Set width/height to native (contentRect x pointPixelScale) versus 1/2 versus 720p on the short side. Write test problems in Notability: fractions, exponents, subscripts, and the - versus = sign at small pen widths. Rate legibility blindly and run RecognizeTextRequest (accurate; en-US and zh-Hans+en) on crops. Record OCR confidence and errors per scale.

Clip buffer. Attach SCClipBufferingOutput; call exportClip with 5, 15 and 20 s (expect a cap at 15). Measure export latency, file size, codec and resolution, the thin-ink artifacts in the clip, the resident memory growth of the buffer at native resolution, and whether buffering continues while backgrounded.

Protected and hidden content. In Safari, play a FairPlay-protected video (for example an Apple TV+ trailer page, if it is FPS) and a normal course video. Verify black regions in captured frames. Check whether Notability or Canvas Student change their UI when sceneCaptureState is active. Record the heuristics for 'possibly_obscured' detection.

Undo versus erase indistinguishability. In Notability, write one stroke, then remove it three ways: squeeze-and-hold whole eraser, partial eraser, and 2-finger-tap undo. Show the captured frame sequences side by side, confirming there is no pixel-level discriminator and that fast erase-and-rewrite within one frame interval can be missed. Document this as the justification for the forbidden-claims list.

Background analysis limits. With the app backgrounded during capture, run (a) CPU tile hashing and HEIC/JPEG encoding, (b) Vision RecognizeTextRequest, and (c) a small Core ML model without the continued-processing.inference entitlement. Record errors, CPU fallback and latency. Confirm that Metal work fails with notPermitted.

Our overlay in the composite. With our PencilKit overlay drawing over Safari or Notability, verify our ink appears in captured frames. Measure the time alignment between PKStroke timestamps and SCK displayTime via synchronizationClock, and verify the masking logic that attributes pixel changes to our own strokes.

iPadOS 26 fallback. Build the broadcast upload extension. Measure memory at native iPad frame sizes against the ~50 MB cap, delivered fps, behaviour on a static screen (whether callbacks stop), and the legibility after the downscale needed to stay under the cap. On iPadOS 27, verify the deprecated extension still works in the background (the LensLink claim).

claims.topic: (a) How WebKit implements captureVisibleTab
claims.final_claim: In WebKit main, WebExtensionContext::tabsCaptureVisibleTab first calls requestPermissionToAccessURLs for the active tab's URL, which may surface a permission prompt. It then fails with "either the 'activeTab' permission or granted host permissions for the current website are required" unless the extension has permission. WebExtensionTab::captureVisibleWebpage behaves differently depending on the browser. (a) If the browser app does NOT implement the WKWebExtensionTab takeSnapshot delegate, WebKit calls WKWebView takeSnapshot with rect = webView.bounds. On macOS it subtracts _topContentInset; on iOS it does not. (b) If the browser DOES implement the delegate, webView is nil, so the rect passed is derived from a nil view (zero rect), and the browser's own closed-source implementation decides what is captured. Shipping Safari may use path (b), so WebKit source does not establish Safari's capture geometry. The WebProcess parser accepts only 'format' (png|jpeg; default PNG in WebKit main) and 'quality' (default 92). rect/scale are not parsed, and BCD also lists them as unsupported in Safari. MDN BCD says Safari's default format is 'jpeg', which contradicts WebKit main. Always pass {format:'png'} explicitly and check the MIME prefix of the returned data URL. If the snapshot image is nil, WebKit returns an empty data URL constant (emptyDataURLValue) instead of an error, and that must be logged as a gap.

dimensions.design_recommendation:
Proposed A44 status per surface. None of this has been verified on a device; confirm on iPadOS 27.0 (24A437) before any claim.

1. bCourses in Safari with our Safari web extension: an A44 candidate and the primary path. The ink is a content-script <canvas> in the page. The capture is browser.tabs.captureVisibleTab (E4-01..E4-10, E4-23). The documented APIs exist. That the injected ink appears in the capture is inferred from WebKit source. Geometry, toolbar cropping, iframe/video capture and Pencil vs Scribble behaviour all need a device test.

2. Our own in-app WKWebView browser with a PKCanvasView as a sibling view: technically capable of an A44 composite. Page image = takeSnapshot; ink = PKDrawing.transformed(...).image(...), composited in our code, with an optional ScreenCaptureKit in-app capture as a system-side check (E4-11..E4-15). Two decisions for the lead: does an in-app browser count as the 'original screen' (it is not Safari, and cookies and the CalNet login are separate)? And should the ink stay out of the WKWebView subtree, since takeSnapshot on iOS may or may not include it (E4-12)?

3. Canvas Student (native): A44 unsupported. No documented overlay or window-level API exists; ScreenCaptureKit exclusions are macOS-only; PiP is a user-started video window with no input (E4-16, E4-21, E4-22). Only allowed: A45 fallbacks, plus G7 path 2 visual observation via ScreenCaptureKit full-display capture, labelled as pixels only.

4. Notability (native): same as Canvas Student, A44 unsupported.

5. Any ScreenCaptureKit full-display frame where our window is in Slide Over or side by side: always A45 (adjacent), never A44. Mark our own window's region as 'self' in the frame.

6. Safari without our extension: observation only.

Evidence record 'CompositeDeliveryProof', created for every image sent to the AI:
- capture_id
- surface: safari_ext | inapp_wkwebview | sck_inapp | sck_fulldisplay
- capture_api
- compositor: dom_in_page | app_composited | system_capture
- captured_at: UTC plus a monotonic timestamp (for ScreenCaptureKit, also SCStreamFrameInfo.displayTime)
- image: mime, width_px, height_px, byte_len, and sha256 of the exact bytes uploaded (after data-URL decode, before any transport encoding)
- backend_receipt: request_id and the sha256 the backend computes on receipt. 'AI received composite' is true only when this matches the client hash.
- geometry:
  - Safari: document_url, runtime.getDocumentId(), navigation.currentEntry.key, visualViewport {offsetLeft, offsetTop, pageLeft, pageTop, width, height, scale}, scrollX/Y, devicePixelRatio, the fiducial-solved image→CSS affine transform and its residual error
  - WKWebView: contentOffset, zoomScale, pageZoom, obscuredContentInsets, and the content→image transform
  - ScreenCaptureKit: contentRect, contentScale, scaleFactor, status
- strokes:
  - rendered_ids: PKStroke.id or our web stroke UUIDs actually drawn into this image
  - clipped_ids and out_of_view_ids
  - a per-stroke bounding box in image pixels
  - stroke_set_hash (ordered IDs plus point hashes)
- anchors: for each stroke, the anchor kind (element | range | text-quote), a stable selector, a text-quote hash, and the offset inside the anchor
- ink_presence_check: after upload, recompute the stroke-mask coverage in the sent image and record pass/fail
- gaps: capture failures, geometry-unverified, iframe/video/DRM blank regions, frame status idle/blank/suspended, dropped pointer sequences, orphaned anchors
- share_state: active | stopped_by_user | stopped_by_system | extension_disabled | permission_revoked | content_inactive, with timestamp

Rules:
- Freeze strokes as 'orphaned' whenever the documentId, the navigation entry or the anchor node changes. Never reposition them silently.
- The Safari path samples on request (on stroke end, scrollend or explicit ask), not as a stream. The time between samples is a recorded gap.
- The UI shows a visible 'AI sees this' indicator on every surface (Guideline 2.5.14).
- Never infer an external app's undo stack or the learner's reasons from pixels.
experiment_steps_proposed: Setup: iPad on iPadOS 27.0 (24A437) with Safari 27, Xcode 27 (27A266a), and a minimal MV3 Safari web extension. The content script injects a position:fixed canvas with pointer-events toggled and draws 4 corner fiducials. A background service worker calls browser.tabs.captureVisibleTab() when the content script sends a message. Test on a bCourses page with an LTI iframe and an embedded video.

S1, composite inclusion: draw Pencil strokes, capture, decode the data URL, and check whether the strokes and fiducials appear in the image. Repeat at pinch zoom 1x, 2x and 3x, with the toolbar collapsed and expanded, at Page Zoom 50/100/175%, and with Request Desktop Website on and off. Record the image size, the fiducial-solved transform and its residual, and whether the top is cropped or padded.
S2, iframe/video: check whether pixels from the cross-origin LTI iframe, <video> and DRM video (if available) are present, black or blank in the capture. Log the result per region type.

S3, input routing: with the ink layer set to touch-action:none and pen-only handling (pointerType==='pen'), confirm that finger scrolling and taps still operate the live page. Repeat with Scribble on and off, and count dropped or duplicated pointer sequences over 50 fast zig-zag strokes.

S4, change detection: navigate within the Canvas single-page app (next question, next module) and reload. Confirm that navigation 'navigate' events, runtime.getDocumentId() changes, and MutationObserver removal of the anchor node each fire, and that the strokes freeze as orphaned. Insert content above the anchor and confirm that scroll anchoring keeps the ink aligned with element-relative anchors.

S5, extension lifecycle: disable the extension in Settings mid-session, revoke site access, and switch tabs. Record the captureVisibleTab errors and SFSafariExtensionManager.stateOfExtension results, and measure how long the background worker survives between captures.

S6, WKWebView (1): add a PKCanvasView (a) as a subview of WKWebView.scrollView and (b) as a sibling above the WKWebView. Call takeSnapshot with the view on screen, with afterScreenUpdates both true and false, and again with the web view removed from its window. Record whether the ink appears in each case, which confirms or refutes the source-code reading in E4-12.

S7, WKWebView (2): compare takeSnapshot plus our PKDrawing.image composite against drawHierarchy(in:afterScreenUpdates:) (record its Bool return) and against a ScreenCaptureKit presentForCurrentApplication() frame. Measure the pixel difference inside the stroke bounding boxes.

S8, ScreenCaptureKit full display: run Canvas Student or Notability full screen, then with our app in Slide Over and then side by side. Confirm that our window appears in the frames. Log SCStreamFrameInfo contentRect, contentScale, scaleFactor and status (count of idle frames). Stop from the system indicator or Control Center and confirm stream(_:didStopWithError:) delivers the userStopped code. Background the app without the screen-capture mode and confirm missingBackgroundMode or a stop.

S9, PiP transparency: feed an AVSampleBufferDisplayLayer with BGRA frames that are fully transparent except for one stroke. Start PiP from a user tap and photograph or screen-capture the result. Record whether the transparent area shows black, the app underneath, or window chrome, whether the PiP window accepts any Pencil input, and whether the PiP window appears in a ScreenCaptureKit full-display frame.

S10, window transparency: in iPadOS 27 windowed mode and in Slide Over, set clear backgrounds on UIWindow, root view and the scene. Record whether the app underneath shows through. Expected result: it does not.

S11, end-to-end proof: upload each composite and have the backend compute sha256 on receipt. Assert it equals the client hash, then re-run the ink-presence mask check on the received bytes. Deliberately corrupt one upload to confirm the check fails and a gap is recorded.

claims.topic: Apple responsiveness thresholds for latency budgets
claims.final_claim: Apple guidance: a delay under 100 ms in a discrete interaction is rarely noticeable. During continuous interaction such as dragging, 50 ms may be noticeable. Event delivery before the main run loop plus rendering after it 'can add' 10–50 ms even under normal operation, and rendering plus display update 'can add' 16–50 ms. A delay as short as one refresh interval (about 8–16 ms) can cause a hitch. These are rough guidelines, not guaranteed floors.
claims.verifier_note: The quotes come from two articles, not one. The 100 ms, 10–50 ms and 16–50 ms figures are in https://developer.apple.com/documentation/xcode/understanding-hangs-in-your-app ("A delay of less than 100 ms in a discrete user interaction is rarely noticeable"; "can add 10 ms to 50 ms to the overall delay ... even under normal operation"; "can add a delay of 16 ms to 50 ms"). The 50 ms dragging and 8–16 ms hitch figures are in understanding-user-interface-responsiveness. The implication that the display segment 'always carries a floor of about 10–50 ms' overclaims, because Apple says 'can add'. improving-app-responsiveness adds: "The thresholds above are very rough guidelines".

claims.topic: MetricKit in iOS 27: cadence, no energy metric
claims.final_claim: In iOS 27 MetricKit was rebuilt around MetricManager, which exposes metricReports and diagnosticReports as async sequences of Codable reports. Metric reports arrive at most once per day and cover the previous 24 hours. Diagnostics such as hangs and crashes arrive immediately. MXMetricManager and MXMetricPayload are marked deprecated at 27.2. Neither the old nor the new API lists a battery or energy metric. The closest proxies are CPU time and instructions, GPU time, pixel luminance and network bytes.
claims.evidence_excerpt: "The system delivers metric reports about the previous 24 hours to your app at most once per day. Diagnostic reports arrive immediately in iOS 15 and later" / MetricManager: iOS 27.0; "metricReports — An asynchronous sequence that delivers daily metric reports." / WWDC26: "In iOS 27, the framework has been rebuilt from the ground up with a contextually rich and expressive modern Swift-first API."

claims.topic: StateReporting splits only some metrics by state
claims.final_claim: With StateReporting (iOS 27) and MetricManager(enabledStateReportingDomains:), MetricReport.stateEntries aggregate a subset of metrics per recorded state. Apple's list is non-exhaustive ('including'): hang time, hitch time, termination counts, signpost intervals, location activity time and app runtime. CPU time, memory, network, disk I/O, GPU, launch and disk space appear only in intervalEntries. With state reporting enabled, intervalEntries also contain shorter sub-interval entries, each with a duration (no start timestamp) and a `states` list of all states active during it. This allows coarse attribution of CPU and network to a path when a sub-interval falls entirely within one state; sub-interval length is undocumented. Instruments shows state transitions in Points of Interest.
claims.verifier_note: stateEntries doc: "Only a subset of metrics appear in state entries, including hang time, hitch time...". The wording is 'including', not an exhaustive list. metrickit/metricreport/intervalentry: "When you enable state reporting, intervalEntries contains shorter sub-interval entries in addition to the full-day entry" and "Each IntervalEntry provides a duration but no start timestamp"; the 'states' topic reads "All states that were active during this collection interval." The implication that per-path CPU and network 'cannot come from MetricKit' is therefore overstated: coarse attribution may be possible, but granularity has to be tested in the field. StateReporting framework page: "Instruments displays transitions in the Points of Interest instrument".

claims.topic: UIDevice.batteryLevel resolution is undocumented
claims.final_claim: UIDevice.batteryLevel ranges from 0.0 to 1.0 when battery monitoring is enabled and is -1.0 otherwise. Its step size is undocumented. Apple does document that batteryLevelDidChangeNotification is sent no more than once per minute, and it explicitly advises against calculating battery drain rate or time remaining from these values.
claims.verifier_note: https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uidevice/batteryleveldidchangenotification (iOS 3.0+): "Notifications for battery level change are sent no more frequently than once per minute. Don't attempt to calculate battery drainage rate or battery time remaining; drainage rate can change frequently depending on built-in applications as well as your application." So the update cadence is partly documented (at most one notification per minute), and a 10 s poll adds nothing beyond that. Apple's warning against computing drain rate undercuts using batteryLevel soaks as a comparative power measure. The step size still needs a device test, so the status is mixed: cadence documented, step size undocumented_needs_device_test.

claims.topic: Established methods for end-to-end latency on touch and pen
claims.final_claim: Casiez et al. (UIST 2017) measured tap latency end to end with a finger-mounted vibration sensor and a photodiode on the screen. The '≥ ~50 ms, mostly from the display' result comes from the paper's abstract as indexed by search engines; the authors' page does not state it. Annett et al. (GI 2014, 'How Low Should We Go?') found that latency perception while inking is ~50 ms, meaning participants could tell a 7 ms baseline apart from roughly 50–61 ms, versus ~2–7 ms for non-inking tasks. The paper also notes devices of that time had 60–120 ms of ink delay. 9to5Mac (press, 2019-06-06) relays Apple's announced drop from 20 ms to 9 ms. Apple's own WWDC19 session gives no millisecond figure, only 'industry-leading, low latency' and predicted touches.
claims.verifier_note: https://gery.casiez.net/turbotouch/lagmeter/lagmeterUIST17.php confirms the method but contains no latency numbers. ACM DL returned 403 and HAL returned Access Denied, so the 50 ms statement is verified only through search-index abstract snippets. Annett abstract extracted from the PDF: "latency perception while inking is worse (~50 milliseconds) than perception while performing non-inking tasks reported previously (~2-7 milliseconds)". WWDC19-221 'Introducing PencilKit': "the same industry-leading, low latency"; "we have robots testing it continuously"; "You should be using predicted touches to reduce your latency even further." The 9 ms figure is press-only and dates to 2018 iPad Pro hardware.

claims.topic: On-device clocks for latency segments
claims.final_claim: CACurrentMediaTime is derived from mach_absolute_time. UITouch.timestamp is seconds since system startup, the same base as ProcessInfo.systemUptime, which counts only awake time. mach_absolute_time does not advance while the device sleeps. ContinuousClock and mach_continuous_time keep counting through sleep; SuspendingClock does not. CMClockGetHostTimeClock is documented as using mach_absolute_time on macOS. From these definitions: touch, display-link and capture timestamps share an uptime base that stops during sleep, while ContinuousClock instants drift away from it across any sleep.
claims.os_sdk: CACurrentMediaTime iOS 2.0+; UITouch.timestamp iOS 2.0+; ContinuousClock/SuspendingClock iOS 16.0+; CMClockGetHostTimeClock iOS 6.0+
claims.evidence_excerpt: CACurrentMediaTime: "A CFTimeInterval derived by calling mach_absolute_time() and converting the result to seconds." UITouch.timestamp: "the time, in seconds since system startup". mach_absolute_time: "this clock does not increment while the system is asleep." ContinuousClock: "does not stop incrementing while the system is asleep." CMClockGetHostTimeClock: "In macOS, the host time clock uses mach_absolute_time".

SCFrameStatus values are complete, idle (display did not change), blank (display is blank), suspended, started and stopped. SCStreamFrameInfo.dirtyRects is only available on macOS and Mac Catalyst. The macOS header describes displayTime as a uint64 mach absolute time; that it is the same on iOS is an inference.

claims.final_claim: Hylog (arXiv 2601.17753; v1 2026-01-25, v2 2026-08-01) combines analytical keylogging (Inputlog) with ecological text logging of rendered text (plug-ins for Word and Chrome). A hybridizer module post-processes both logs offline and merges them into a unified dual-track log, or 'dual trace'. It targets IME typing, not handwriting. Kollberg and Severinson Eklundh (2002, 'Studying Writers' Revising Patterns with S-Notation Analysis') and Conijn et al. ('A Product- and Process-Oriented Tagset for Revisions in Writing', Written Communication 39(1), online 2021-10-29) provide revision representation and labelling schemes. dimensions.design_recommendation:
EXPERIMENT PLAN P0-11/E3: measuring the two capture paths against a human reference process. Everything below is proposed. Items marked [device] need a real iPad on iPadOS 27.0 (24A437); items marked [Mac] need Xcode/Instruments 27.

1) Ground truth, built without the product.
(a) Scripted synthetic cases. A performer follows a card per case, so the true event list is known by design.
(b) External camera. An iPhone at 240 fps slo-mo on a fixed overhead mount records the screen, hand and Pencil (E3-13).
(c) Built-in Control Center screen recording (E3-11) as the screen-pixel reference. If a Mac is present and the run is not a power run, QuickTime tethered recording is the alternative (E3-12).
(d) Two annotators label the video independently in ELAN, one tier per event class, then adjudicate. Report Cohen's kappa for event type and a boundary tolerance of ±100 ms (E3-24).
(e) Synchronization. The app shows a clapper: a full-screen flash plus a QR code with a session-relative counter, at the start, every 60 s, and at the end. Fit the offset and linear drift between camera or recording frames and the app timeline, and report the residual.
The product's own logs are the object under test and are never ground truth.

2) Clocks. Put every on-device stamp in one uptime base: CACurrentMediaTime, UITouch.timestamp, CADisplayLink.targetTimestamp and SCStreamFrameInfo.displayTime (the last one is [device] to confirm). Store a paired ContinuousClock reading with each entry to detect sleep. The server measures its own segments with its own monotonic clock. Only durations and session-relative offsets leave the device, per privacy reason 35F9.1 (E3-15, E3-19).
Latency segments:
- t0: pen-up (camera frame and UITouch timestamp).
- t1: evidence available. For S, the PKCanvasView drawing-change callback. For V, the SCK sample-buffer callback, with frame age measured as t1 minus displayTime.
- t2: sync acknowledged by the server.
- t3: recognition done.
- t4: reasoning done.
- t5: response received on device.
- t6: displayed (display-link target) and photon (camera).
Wrap each segment in an OSSignposter interval so traces and Run Comparisons line up [Mac] (E3-03).

3) Cases: 40 labelled synthetic cases. S = own PencilKit canvas; V = external app (Notability, Canvas Student, Safari/bCourses) through SCK.
Writes and erases:
- P01 linear 4-step solution (S, V)
- P02 quick erase: write a step, erase it within 1 s (S, V)
- P03 partial pixel-erase of one digit, then rewrite (S, V)
- P04 lasso-delete 3 strokes (S, V)
- P05 lasso-move a step with no content change (S, V)
- P06 scribble cross-out, then rewrite beside it (S, V)
- P07 overwrite one digit in place (S, V)
- P08 insert a step between lines (S, V)
Undo and redo:
- P09 single undo (S; V may only record "content disappeared")
- P10 undo ×5, then redo ×2 (S, V)
- P11 undo, then a new stroke, which truncates the redo branch (S, V)
- P12 undo of an erase (S, V)
- P13 Notability gesture undo vs toolbar undo (V only; must not be labelled "undo")
- P14 toggle undo/redo 6 times in 2 s (S, V)
Branches and retries:
- P15 attempt A crossed out, attempt B beside it (S, V)
- P16 attempt A fully erased, attempt B in the same place (S, V)
- P17 two methods side by side, then circle one (S, V)
- P18 resume A after B (S, V)
- P19 copy a step, then modify it (S, V)
- P20 wrong answer, then AI hint, then corrected retry (S, V)
Anchors and navigation:
- P21 scroll one screen mid-solution (S, V)
- P22 pinch-zoom 2×, write, zoom out (S, V)
- P23 page switch and back (S, V)
- P24 problem change in Canvas Student or bCourses (V; S equivalent)
- P25 app switch Safari → Notability → Safari (V)
- P26 rotation or Split View resize (S, V)
Visibility and staleness:
- P27 palm resting over the writing for 5 s: physical occlusion only, so the expected result is no gap in screen capture; verify it [device]
- P28 notification banner or Control Center over the work (V)
- P29 our own UI covering external content (V)
- P30 keyboard covering the lower half (V)
- P31 burst of 12 strokes in 3 s (S, V)
- P32 faint 1 pt ink (S, V)
- P33 idle 60 s: idle frames, so "no change", not a gap (S, V)
- P34 FairPlay or otherwise protected content, giving blank or blacked-out frames, so a gap (V)
Interruptions:
- P35 offline 30 s, then reconnect (S, V)
- P36 our app backgrounded 20 s (S, V)
- P37 screen lock 15 s (S, V)
- P38 user stops sharing via system UI, restart after 20 s: SCK userStopped, hard gap (V)
- P39 Low Power Mode, 10-min session (S, V)
- P40 10-min composite session for power and cost (S, V)
Each case gets a ground-truth event list (type, t_start, t_end, region, key-step flag, branch id, expected gap intervals) and runs at least 5 times per path.

4) Metrics per path.
- Key-step retention: matched ground-truth key steps divided by all ground-truth key steps (±300 ms, region IoU ≥ 0.5). Report transient steps (erased within 2 s) separately.
- Hallucinated-step rate.
- Order accuracy: Kendall's tau plus normalized Levenshtein distance over event types.
- Branch accuracy: F1 on step-to-branch assignment and on parent edges.
- Before/after version completeness.
- Gap recall and gap precision against ground-truth unobservable intervals.
- Forbidden-inference count: V-path claims of undo, redo, reasons or an undo stack. This must be 0.
- Freshness: evidence age at each AI decision, plus the share of stale evidence that was not flagged.
- Latency: p50, p90 and p99 per segment and end to end, with the camera cross-check.
- Power: Power Profiler per-app CPU/GPU/display/network impact and system share of battery per hour. One iPad model, unplugged, fixed brightness, 3 repeats per path [Mac to analyze]. Thermal state logged throughout (E3-01, E3-02).
- Cost: bytes and frames uploaded per minute, model input and output tokens, and dollars per case and per hour.
Field (pilot) data: MetricManager with a StateReporting domain capturePath=S|V gives hitch, hang and signpost-segment metrics per path. CPU, network and GPU are not available per state (E3-06, E3-07).

5) Proposed acceptance targets, to be set by the lead:
- S: key-step retention ≥ 0.98 and order tau ≥ 0.95.
- V: key-step retention ≥ 0.85 and gap recall ≥ 0.95.
- Both: forbidden inferences = 0, and every share-stop and blank interval recorded as a gap.
Owned-canvas, frozen-capture and side-by-side runs are A45 fallbacks and are never reported as R59/A44.

6) Not available, and why the plan works around it:
- No configurable SCK frame rate, queue depth or dirty rects on iOS (E3-17, E3-16).
- No per-case energy from MetricKit, Organizer or Settings > Battery (E3-06, E3-08, E3-09).
- Power Profiler values are relative, model-specific, and read 0 while charging (E3-02).
- Screen-recording fps and resolution are undocumented (E3-11).
- Instruments analysis requires a Mac (E3-01, E3-03, E3-04).
experiment_steps_proposed: [device] Put the test iPad on iPadOS 27.0 (24A437) and enable Developer Mode (this needs one Xcode pairing, so a Mac once). Turn on Settings > Developer > Hang Detection, and Performance Trace in Power Profiler mode with the test app toggled on. Add the Performance Trace and Screen Recording controls to Control Center.

[device] Characterize the reference recorder. Run the app's clock test pattern (a counter updated on every CADisplayLink frame at 120 Hz on a ProMotion iPad) under Control Center screen recording for 1, 5 and 20 minutes. Extract per-frame PTS, average and minimum fps, resolution and codec with ffprobe. Repeat while the app's SCK picker stream is active, and record whether both can run together and whether sceneCaptureState changes.

[device] Characterize the external camera. Mount an iPhone (240 fps slo-mo) overhead. Film the clapper (flash plus QR code with a session-relative counter) at start, every 60 s and at end. Fit offset and drift against the app log and report the residual in ms.

[device] Clock validation. For 1000 S-path strokes, log UITouch.timestamp, CACurrentMediaTime at the delegate callback and ContinuousClock. For V-path frames, log displayTime, CMSampleBuffer PTS and CACurrentMediaTime at the callback. Confirm the shared uptime base and measure callback lag. Repeat across a 15 s screen lock (P37) to measure the divergence between ContinuousClock and uptime.

[device] Measure SCK cadence on iOS 27. For cases P31 (burst), P33 (idle), P21/P22 (scroll/zoom) and P34 (protected content), record the frame callback intervals and the counts of each SCFrameStatus (complete/idle/blank/suspended/stopped). Confirm that a palm over the glass (P27) changes no captured pixels.

[device] Write the 40 case cards (P01–P40) with scripted timing. A performer runs each case at least 5 times on the S path (own PencilKit canvas) and on the V path (Notability, Canvas Student, Safari/bCourses under SCK), while the camera and the reference screen recording run.

[offline] Two annotators independently label the camera and screen-recording video in ELAN, with one tier per event class (write, erase, lasso, undo, redo, cross-out, branch, navigation, occlusion, idle, offline, share-stop, gap). Compute Cohen's kappa for event type and boundary agreement at ±100 ms, then adjudicate into the ground-truth event list. Export as InkML-like JSON.

[offline] Score each run: key-step retention (overall and transient), hallucination rate, Kendall's tau and normalized edit distance, branch F1, before/after completeness, gap recall and precision, forbidden-inference count (must be 0 on V), freshness (evidence age at each AI decision), and latency p50/p90/p99 per segment from the OSSignposter-bracketed app log plus the camera-measured photon time.

[device→Mac] Power runs. Use one iPad model, unplugged, fixed brightness, and a cool start (record thermalState). Run P40 (10-min composite) 3 times per path with the on-device Power Profiler, AirDrop the .aar to a Mac, and compare per-app CPU/GPU/display/network impact in Instruments 27, including Run Comparisons on the signpost intervals. As a sanity check, run 60-minute soaks logging UIDevice.batteryLevel every 10 s to find its real step size.

[offline] Cost accounting. For each case, record bytes and frames uploaded, images per minute after the app-side downsampling policy (SCK frame rate is not configurable on iOS), model input and output tokens and dollars, and normalize per case and per hour.

[pilot, TestFlight] Ship MetricManager with a StateReporting domain capturePath=S|V and OSSignposter/mxSignpost segment intervals. Collect daily reports for hitch, hang and signpost duration per state. CPU, network and GPU come only as interval entries, not per state. Check the Xcode Organizer Battery and Energy panes once enough opted-in usage has accumulated.
[report] Give each result a label (documented/inferred/device-measured) and keep A45 fallback runs (owned canvas, frozen capture, side-by-side) separate from anything claimed under R59/A44.
